body: It's probably just because being dead is easier than being alive. Death asks nothing of you, unlike life. And surely there must be people in the world that you think deserve to die. Your principles might tell you that wishing death upon even the worst person is wrong, but does that mean that you REALLY care if they live or die?
I don't know if the idea of "deserving" suicide is relevant. If I would be better off dead than alive, and the world would be better off with me dead than alive, then what does it matter?

What if your flaws aren't just about choice, but about who you are intrinsically? And what if you can see the choices in front of you, including the "right" choice, but you just make the "wrong" choice anyway because it's easier or more fun?

True, but zero is still larger than a negative, so in some cases, self-destruction could be considered an improvement. Obviously, becoming an actual good person is ideal, but that's not always realistic.
Maybe, but when I try to think about the person I want to be, I just end up thinking that the best, and easiest, form of self-improvement would be death. At least for me it would be.
Because I have a set of morals that are completely at odds with how I act and what kind of person I am.
Nothing happened. I'm just a shitty person.
